how_to_read: Keys are paths relative to this folder. result valid | invalid (id = section 15 id) | table (rows carry their own results). 'normalized' lists fields a reader must produce after defaults. Transcripts are checked by the 'final' assertions plus the step list.

config/hideout.anchor-overlaps-root-exac.note: A user anchor names an id inside the hideout.* root scope.

config/hideout.anchor-overlaps-root.toml.note: A user anchor's scope covers foxglove.*, a root scope.

config/invalid-folder-url.toml.note: A folder source with a url (v1.1).

config/invalid-source-id.toml.note: A source id with uppercase and underscore (v1.1).

config/invalid-unknown-anchor.toml.note: A source names an anchor that is not listed (v1.1).

config/hideout.valid.toml.note: Public catalog source, private git and folder sources, a developer-mode folder without anchor, a user anchor with a non-overlapping scope.

frames/panel-frames.json.note: Each frame carries its own expect; length mismatches are dropped.

channels/channel-wire.json.note: (v1.4, #977) The channel wire: the nonce as the first frame, u32 LE framing, the 64 MiB and 256-byte caps, and which pipe names a consumer connects to. Rows carry their own expect; the Rust and Python readers both pass them.

legacy/invalid-new-key-hub.plugin.toml.note: hub is new; a legacy file cannot use it.

legacy/invalid-new-key-visibility.plugin.note: A legacy file must not contain keys new in this spec.

legacy/invalid-one-label-id.plugin.toml.note: Legacy ids are reverse-DNS (two or more labels).

legacy/invalid-settings-min-above-max.pl.note: An int setting's min above its max is refused (fuzz finding 2: clamp used to panic).

legacy/kit-old-name.kit.toml.note: kit.toml (the name before the rename) reads the same as plugin.toml.

legacy/plugin-foxglove-prefix.plugin.tom.note: foxglove.* ids are family foxglove too.

legacy/plugin-org-foxglove.plugin.toml.note: org.foxglove.* maps to family foxglove; api 1.13 stays a foxglove api.

legacy/plugin-third-party.plugin.toml.note: A third-party reverse-DNS plugin.toml. Legacy Provides value facts is still read.

legacy/plugin-with-contributions.plugin..note: Legacy actions, secrets and settings keep their meaning; every legacy Provides value reads.

legacy/precedence-kit-only/.note: Reader looks for module.toml, then plugin.toml, then kit.toml.

legacy/precedence-module-over-plugin/.note: Reader looks for module.toml, then plugin.toml, then kit.toml.

legacy/precedence-plugin-over-kit/.note: Reader looks for module.toml, then plugin.toml, then kit.toml.

manifests/invalid/activation-unknown-eve.note: Activation is events only, never timers.

manifests/invalid/family-label-vs-family.note: vulpes.* with family foxglove: label and family disagree.

manifests/invalid/family-reserved-label-.note: A reserved first label needs the matching family.

manifests/invalid/hub-newer-minor.toml.note: Written for a newer minor than a v1.0 reader serves. (v1.4: this reader serves 1.1, so the vector says 1.2.)

manifests/invalid/mcp-duplicate-name.tom.note: Tool names are unique in the module.

manifests/invalid/mcp-method-not-provide.note: The tool's method is outside the module's provides (v1.1).

manifests/invalid/provides-content-missi.note: content module without a content: entry.

manifests/invalid/provides-firmware-miss.note: firmware module without a firmware: entry.

manifests/invalid/requires-public-needs-.note: Public module requiring a private one. Index context tells the reader example.private.notes is private.

manifests/invalid/run-absolute-service.t.note: Absolute run is for adopted only.

manifests/invalid/run-parent-dir.toml.note: run[0] must stay in the version folder.

manifests/invalid/syntax-wrong-type.toml.note: run must be an array of strings; a string is the wrong type.

manifests/invalid/ui-window-without-perm.note: A [[ui.windows]] entry needs the ui.window permission. v1.1.

manifests/invalid/unknown-key-future-min.note: A key from a future minor with hub left at 1.0 is refused as unknown.

manifests/invalid/unknown-key-nested.tom.note: Unknown key inside a contribution table.

manifests/invalid/visibility-private-res.note: A private module's id must not start with a reserved first label.

manifests/valid/activation-all-events.to.note: Every activation event form (device:<class> is short for fact:devices.present.<class>).

manifests/valid/api-arete-alias.toml.note: arete is an alias of vulpes in family and api keys; readers write vulpes. One-label id vulpes is first-party only. adopted run[0] is absolute.

manifests/valid/content-board-profile.to.note: content kind: no run, at least one content: entry.

manifests/valid/contrib-mcp-tools.toml.note: A read tool and a time-limited write tool (ttl_max_s <= 600).

manifests/valid/contrib-ui-all-slots.tom.note: All five panel slots plus a module window (needs ui.window).

manifests/valid/firmware.toml.note: firmware kind: no run, at least one firmware: entry.

manifests/valid/hub-1-0.toml.note: hub 1.0 is served by a v1.0 reader (same major, server minor >= client minor).

manifests/valid/id-arete-prefix.toml.note: Reserved first label arete (alias) matches family vulpes; the reader writes vulpes.

manifests/valid/id-legacy-prefix-org-fox.note: The legacy prefix org.foxglove. is family foxglove.

manifests/valid/private.toml.note: Private module: reverse-DNS under a placeholder name, no reserved first label, may require a public module.

manifests/valid/requires-forms.toml.note: Bare id, and versions shortened to MAJOR or MAJOR.MINOR.

manifests/valid/runtime-with-pin.toml.note: runtime: no run, [[pin]] allowed (placeholder hash and .invalid host).

manifests/valid/service-full.toml.note: The spec's example (4.2), with placeholder ids.

manifests/valid/service-minimal.toml.note: Smallest service: only the required keys. Every default applies.

manifests/valid/version-prerelease.toml.note: SemVer with a prerelease and no +build.

manifests/valid/when-clauses.toml.note: when: one fact name, optionally prefixed by !.

panels/invalid/one-bad-one-good.json.note: Over a cap rejects that panel; the others register (rejected list in the ui.register result).

panels/invalid/over-canvas-shapes.json.note: 5000 canvas shapes ('a few hundred' is the cap; also over the 2000-node cap, 5.5).

panels/invalid/over-depth.json.note: Depth 40, over the depth cap of 32 and under the 128 message-nesting cap (5.5, v1.1).

panels/invalid/over-message-nesting.json.note: A message nested 5000 deep (objects in objects), over the 128 message-nesting cap (5.5, v1.1.1). Refused before parsing; a reader must not recurse or overflow.

panels/invalid/over-nodes.json.note: 3000 nodes in one panel, over the 2000-node cap (5.5, v1.1).

panels/invalid/over-string-length.json.note: One 120000-character string, over the 16 KiB text cap (5.5, v1.1).

panels/valid/all-node-types.json.note: Every layout and widget type once, a bind, and streams on canvas and text.

panels/valid/under-caps-canvas-200.json.note: A canvas with 200 shapes ('a few hundred' is the cap; 200 is comfortably under).

panels/valid/under-caps-small.json.note: A tiny tree, far under every cap.

panels/valid/unknown-node-type.json.note: registers; the unknown node draws as 'needs a newer Hideout' (5.2)

permissions/permissions.json.note: Each row is its own vector. result valid | invalid (with id) | never (with id permission.never, depending on context). 'sensitive' lists the red-dialog strings (6.1).

transcripts/facts/hub-state-facts.json.note: Facts the hub publishes: module.<id>.state, .reason, .version, hub.safe_mode.

transcripts/facts/set-denied.json.note: facts.set without facts.write:<pattern> or a facts: provides entry answers error 5; device.* is never writable.

transcripts/facts/set-subscribe-changed..note: facts.set from a provider, facts.subscribe by a reader, facts.changed notification ({subscription, key, value}).

transcripts/gpu/ending-reservation-needs.note: A gaming reservation changes only through the user's own click (action.invoke or ui.event with a user source); no method can end it.

transcripts/gpu/request-release.json.note: gpu.request / gpu.release / gpu.changed on the Vulpes module; error 3 while reserved for gaming; a gaming reservation is never a method.

transcripts/hub/bisect.json.note: Find the module that breaks Hideout: from safe mode the hub halves the enabled set until one module is left; the saved enabled set is never edited.

transcripts/hub/hub-gone-grace.json.note: With no hub back within 30 s, each module exits cleanly (lights handed back, the Info screen handed back).

transcripts/hub/hub-restart-takes-back.j.note: The hub restarts after a panic and takes back running modules: each reconnects with initialize and its original token; the hub checks pid and exe hash.

transcripts/hub/quarantine-breadcrumb.js.note: Two hub restarts within a minute with the same panel breadcrumb start the hub with that module's panels quarantined.

transcripts/hub/safe-mode-not-triggered..note: Three hub restarts spread over more than five minutes do not trigger safe mode.

transcripts/hub/safe-mode.json.note: After three hub restarts in five minutes the hub starts in safe mode: only the Modules page, no module started, hub.safe_mode true.

transcripts/lifecycle/activation-by-call.note: activation.on contains call: the hub starts the module, then routes the call once it is ready.

transcripts/lifecycle/bad-hub-version.js.note: A hub minor the hub does not serve (1.9 against 1.0) gets error 7 and the connection closes.

transcripts/lifecycle/call-timeout.json.note: A call with no answer fails after 30 s on the caller's side (error 4).

transcripts/lifecycle/duplicate-request-.note: (v1.2) A duplicate in-flight request id answers -32600 rpc.duplicate-request-id with id null; the first call still completes.

transcripts/lifecycle/initialize-bad-tok.note: A module with a wrong launch token is refused (error 5) and the connection is dropped.

transcripts/lifecycle/initialize-first.j.note: initialize comes first on every connection; anything else first answers error 5 (denied).

transcripts/lifecycle/initialize-hub-not.note: A client whose hub major is not served gets error 7 (version) and the connection closes.

transcripts/lifecycle/initialize-module..note: A module connects with its launch token; the hub checks token, pid and exe hash and answers with granted and the served versions.

transcripts/lifecycle/initialize-tool.js.note: An outside tool connects without a token and is approved once; the grant is what the user approved.

transcripts/lifecycle/late-reply-after-t.note: Error 4 after 30 s, then the module's late result is dropped.

transcripts/lifecycle/lease-addressed-ev.note: (v1.3) A provider event with params.to naming a lease goes only to that lease's holder; another consumer gets nothing; after release the address is dead and the event is dropped.

transcripts/lifecycle/lease-closed-disco.note: (v1.3) A consumer's connection ends while it holds a lease: the provider gets lease.closed {lease, reason: disconnect}.

transcripts/lifecycle/lease-closed-relea.note: (v1.3) A consumer releases a lease: the hub forwards the release call, then sends the provider lease.closed {lease, reason: released}.

transcripts/lifecycle/malformed-json.jso.note: A line that is not JSON answers -32700 with id null.

transcripts/lifecycle/module-crash-durin.note: The provider crashes mid-call: the caller gets error 2, once.

transcripts/lifecycle/oversized-line.jso.note: (v1.2) A line over 256 KiB answers -32600 rpc.frame-too-large with id null, the channel closes, the supervisor counts one crash.

transcripts/lifecycle/ping.json.note: ping is a call with empty params and result.

transcripts/lifecycle/provider-not-runni.note: A provided method whose module is not running answers error 2 (after activation by call, if declared).

transcripts/lifecycle/rate-limited.json.note: Error 8 is rate-limited. Example: ui.patch beyond ~20/s per panel is coalesced, not errored (5.3); a method may still answer 8.

transcripts/lifecycle/re-registration-re.note: A new instance after a crash restart registers again; the hub replaces the module's panels in one step and keeps view state by node id.

transcripts/lifecycle/register-not-ready.note: A module that does not send module.ready within 30 s of start is treated as crashed.

transcripts/lifecycle/register-ready.jso.note: Registration: module.register (one method rejected because the catalog does not allow it), ui.register, module.ready. Only after ready does the router send traffic.

transcripts/lifecycle/register-undeclare.note: ui.register with a panel id not declared in [[ui.panels]] is rejected (ui.undeclared); declared ones register.

transcripts/lifecycle/unknown-method.jso.note: A method no module provides answers -32601.

transcripts/mcp/tools-exposed.json.note: hideout mcp exposes <module name>_<tool name>; write tools hold for at most ttl_max_s (<= 600) and the Info screen at most 60 s.

transcripts/modules/disable-required-by..note: Disabling a module an enabled module requires is refused with lifecycle.required-by naming the dependents.

transcripts/modules/manage-denied.json.note: modules.* without modules.manage, or from a client the never-list excludes, answers error 5.

transcripts/modules/private-hidden-from-.note: modules.list over MCP leaves private modules out unless [privacy] agents_see_private is true; facts about them are not sent either.

transcripts/stream/channel-offer-rejecte.note: module.register offering a channel the catalog does not allow lists it under rejected with permission.provider.

transcripts/stream/channel-open-denied.j.note: Without channel.open:<module>/<channel> the hub answers error 5; a keys-class channel over MCP is never granted.

transcripts/stream/channel-open-tool.jso.note: An outside tool opens a channel: the hub checks channel.open:<module>/<channel>, calls channel.create on the provider, returns {pipe, nonce}.

transcripts/stream/channel-create-bad-pi.note: (v1.4, #977) The provider answers channel.create with a pipe that is not a local hideout-ch- pipe. The hub never passes it on: the consumer gets error 6 with data.id channel.pipe.

transcripts/stream/panel-stream-grant.js.note: A live panel (canvas with stream): the hub's panel host opens the module's channel as a normal channel with the same grant. Frames are binary, never JSON, never through the router.

transcripts/supervisor/crash-backoff-and.note: A crashed instance restarts with fixed backoff steps of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 60 s, then 60 s, no jitter (v1.1); five crashes in ten minutes stops it with one notification per module per sign-in. Notices by events only (process handle, pipe close).

transcripts/supervisor/crashes-spread-ou.note: Five crashes spread over more than ten minutes do not stop the module.

transcripts/supervisor/exit-zero-is-stop.note: Exit code 0 is a stop, not a crash; an event-started module that exits 0 is not restarted.

transcripts/supervisor/no-rollback-after.note: Crash-stopped more than ten minutes after an update does not roll back.

transcripts/supervisor/provider-gone-err.note: At runtime a required module that is gone is only 'provider gone': calls get error 2 and the dependent shows Waiting for <module>.

transcripts/supervisor/rollback-after-up.note: A module that reaches crash-stopped within 10 minutes of an update goes back to the previous version by itself and says so.

transcripts/supervisor/root-cause-once.j.note: A state caused by another module says Waiting for <module> and links there; the tray shows only the root. The graph is requires plus channel.open: permissions.

transcripts/supervisor/start-with-defaul.note: Start with default settings renames the settings folder to settings.bad-<time> and starts the module; the hub needs no knowledge of the values.

transcripts/supervisor/state-crash-stopp.note: State crash-stopped: the fact module.<id>.state is 'crash-stopped'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-install-fai.note: State install-failed: the fact module.<id>.state is 'install-failed'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-needs-hub.j.note: State needs-hub: the fact module.<id>.state is 'needs-hub'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-off.json.note: State off: the fact module.<id>.state is 'off'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-quarantined.note: State quarantined: the fact module.<id>.state is 'quarantined'.

final.ui_name: Example Art's page couldn't be shown

transcripts/supervisor/state-restarting..note: State restarting: the fact module.<id>.state is 'restarting'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-running.jso.note: State running: the fact module.<id>.state is 'running'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-starting.js.note: State starting: the fact module.<id>.state is 'starting'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-update-busy.note: State update-busy: the fact module.<id>.state is 'update-busy'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-update-wait.note: State update-waiting: the fact module.<id>.state is 'update-waiting'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-updating.js.note: State updating: the fact module.<id>.state is 'updating'.

transcripts/supervisor/state-waiting.jso.note: State waiting: the fact module.<id>.state is 'waiting'.

transcripts/supervisor/update-waiting-pe.note: An update that adds permissions keeps the old version running and shows Update waiting for you; never a modal at sign-in.

transcripts/swap/caller-error-2-once.jso.note: Callers see at most one error 2 and retry.

transcripts/swap/drain-busy-force.json.note: Drain busy, then the user presses Force: the hub sends module.drain again (user action, not a timer).

transcripts/swap/drain-busy-not-now.json.note: Drain busy, then the user presses Not now: the old version keeps running, nothing more is sent.

transcripts/swap/drain-busy.json.note: Drain answered busy: the swap waits. State update-busy. The hub sends module.drain again only on module.idle, never on a timer.

transcripts/swap/drain-reasons.json.note: module.drain reasons: update, rollback, reload, disable, remove.

transcripts/swap/handover-export-null.js.note: state.export may answer null: no state.import is sent.

transcripts/swap/handover.json.note: Hot swap, swap=handover: drain, state.export on the old (blob up to 256 KiB or null), module.exit, start the new, state.import, then register and ready.

transcripts/swap/key-action-during-swap..note: A key action during a swap is queued up to 2 s and delivered once, or dropped with a named status line.

transcripts/swap/overlap.json.note: Hot swap, swap=overlap: stage, drain (done), start the new beside the old, route new calls on its module.ready, exit the old.

final.header_text: Updating... for at most a second

transcripts/ui/action-invoke.json.note: action.invoke from key, tray, palette and panel.

transcripts/ui/badge.json.note: ui.badge (v1.3): attention, count (99+), dirty asks before close, none; unknown panel ignored.

transcripts/ui/patch-event-asset.json.note: ui.patch (notification) set/insert/remove; ui.event refused with data.reason (hub reverts optimistic input); ui.asset.put by SHA-256.

transcripts/ui/patch-rate.json.note: Patches above ~20/s per panel are coalesced by the hub (no error).

transcripts/ui/settings-get-set.json.note: The hub reads and writes settings only through settings.get and settings.set; a refusal carries data.reason.

transcripts/ui/visibility.json.note: ui.visibility (v1.3): visible, hidden, closed, sent on change; streams close when not visible. (v1.4) tile panels too: visible while the tray panel is open.

transcripts/ui/window-open.json.note: A module window: the hub shows an Open button and sends ui.window.open (needs ui.window).

trust/catalogs/foxglove.alias-kits.catal.note: 'kits' is read as an alias of modules.

trust/catalogs/foxglove.alias-plugins.ca.note: 'plugins' is read as an alias of modules.

trust/catalogs/foxglove.catalog.json.note: Family catalog; also lists a third-party public module under a scope the root grants foxglove (12.3). Offers a channel with its capability line.

trust/catalogs/foxglove.with-revocations.note: Revocations alongside entries; yank versions 0.1.0, revoke 0.2.0.

trust/catalogs/hideout.catalog.json.note: Offers a keys-class channel; the permission dialog must show its capability line (6.2).

trust/catalogs/invalid/entry-out-of-scop.note: One out-of-scope entry rejects the whole catalog.

trust/catalogs/invalid/epoch.catalog.jso.note: Catalog epoch is not the root's.

trust/catalogs/invalid/mismatch-kind.cat.note: Entry kind (content) differs from the manifest in trust/folders/foxglove.example-art-0.4.0 (service).

trust/catalogs/invalid/mismatch-visibili.note: Entry visibility (private) differs from the manifest (public).

trust/catalogs/invalid/private-in-public.note: A public source's modules must be public; a public catalog MUST NOT list a private one.

trust/catalogs/invalid/revocation-out-of.note: Revocation ids must be in the family scope too.

trust/catalogs/invalid/unlisted-key.cata.note: Valid minisign signature, but by a key the root does not list for foxglove.

trust/catalogs/invalid/user-catalog-firs.note: A user anchor's scope is example.private.*; a first-party id is out of scope.

trust/catalogs/invalid/user-catalog-in-p.note: A private module's entry offered by a source declared public.

trust/catalogs/invalid/wrong-family-key..note: Signed by the vulpes key; each key is bound to one family.

trust/catalogs/legacy.foxglove-plugin-ca.note: Foxglove's v2 catalog verifies under the legacy root (one family, foxglove). Placeholder hashes.

trust/catalogs/user-private.catalog.json.note: A user-anchored catalog: no root.json above it, no family key; an absent family reads as user (12.4, v1.1).
trust/catalogs/user-private.catalog.json.grants_note: may be granted key.events/hid.raw/keys channels with the red warning, never over MCP (13.6)

trust/install/folder-changed-file.note: example-art.exe content differs from the signed hash.

trust/install/folder-exact.note: The folder trust/folders/foxglove.example-art-0.4.0 holds exactly the signed files; installing it grants nothing (6.5).

trust/install/folder-extra-file.note: Same folder plus an extra file extra.dll (listed here, not on disk, to keep the folder clean): not exactly the signed files.

trust/install/install-revoked.note: Version 0.2.0 is revoked: no install, and a running copy stops.

trust/install/install-unknown-archive.note: Archive trust/archives/foxglove.example-art-0.4.0.zip offered to a reader whose accepted catalogs are only vulpes.

trust/install/install-yanked.note: Version 0.1.0 is yanked: no new installs (an installed copy keeps running).

trust/install/no-dev-mode-outside-catalo.note: A module folder outside any catalog, developer mode off (v1.1).

trust/install/sideload-first-party-id.note: Developer mode, source sideload: foxglove.example-art is in a first-party scope.

trust/install/sideload-own-id.note: Developer mode, source sideload: example.private.notes is outside every first-party scope.

trust/install/sideload-hideout-scope-vio.note: The module identifier falls within a registered first-party scope and cannot be sideloaded directly.

trust/install/archive-extract-valid.note: The archive contains exactly the files and hashes declared in the accepted catalog.

trust/install/install-catalog-expired-by.note: A valid catalog whose expiry has passed by the clock: install is refused (trust.expired).

trust/install/install-root-bad-signature.note: The root document fails cryptographic verification against the pinned key.

trust/root/root.bad-signature.json.note: Signed by a key that is not the pinned root key.

trust/root/root.key-reuse.json.note: One key listed in two families.

trust/root/root.legacy-foxglove-plugin-r.note: Foxglove's own root format stays readable. Family scope is exactly foxglove.* and org.foxglove.* (4.10, v1.1).
trust/root/root.legacy-foxglove-plugin-r.note2: read as a root with one family, foxglove

panels/valid/tone-value-and-label.json.note: tone (v1.4) on value and label: the six words, and an unknown word, which registers and draws as neutral.

panels/invalid/tone-not-string.json.note: tone (v1.4) must be a string; a number rejects that panel.

panels/valid/button-opens.json.note: button opens (v1.4): page, page#<node id> and settings, the module's own panels only.

panels/invalid/button-opens-other-module.note: opens (v1.4) names only the module's own page, a node in it, or its settings.

panels/invalid/button-opens-empty-node.j.note: page#<node id> (v1.4) needs a node id.

panels/invalid/button-opens-and-action.j.note: A button (v1.4) has opens or action, not both.

panels/valid/button-action.json.note: button action (v1.4) names one of the module's [[actions]]: the hub sends action.invoke (source panel) and shows the bound key.

panels/invalid/button-action-unknown.jso.note: button action (v1.4) naming no [[actions]] entry rejects that panel.

panels/invalid/button-action-bad-id.json.note: button action (v1.4) is an action id (a-z, 0-9, -).

panels/valid/tile-at-caps.json.note: A tile at every tile cap (v1.4): 12 nodes, depth 3, one button, a 64-byte string.

panels/invalid/tile-over-nodes.json.note: 13 nodes in a tile, over the tile cap of 12 (v1.4).

panels/invalid/tile-over-depth.json.note: Depth 4 in a tile, over the tile cap of 3 (v1.4).

panels/invalid/tile-two-buttons.json.note: Two buttons in a tile, over the tile cap of one (v1.4).

panels/invalid/tile-over-text.json.note: A 65-byte string in a tile, over the tile text cap of 64 bytes (v1.4).

panels/invalid/tile-bad-page-good.json.note: The same 65-byte string: over the tile cap, far under the page cap (v1.4). Only the tile is rejected.

manifests/valid/setting-file.toml.note: kind = "file" settings (v1.4, hub 1.1), with and without a filter; the default is a path string, "" for none.

manifests/invalid/setting-file-hub-1-0.t.note: kind = "file" is new in hub 1.1 (v1.4): a manifest using it says hub = "1.1", so a 1.0 reader refuses it.

manifests/invalid/setting-filter-path.to.note: A filter (v1.4) is file-name patterns only: no folders or drive.

manifests/invalid/setting-file-default-n.note: A file setting's default is a path string (v1.4).

legacy/invalid-setting-kind-file.plugin..note: kind = "file" (v1.4) is module.toml only; a legacy file keeps plugin.toml's three kinds.

manifests/valid/stdio-module-with-panels.note: A legacy plugin's module.toml (v1.4): the stdio transport kept, a tile and a page declared, an icon from the published list and one that is not (draws the generic icon), and a tile shown once its app was seen (apps.seen.<name>, an optional fact).

manifests/invalid/when-apps-seen-with-ex.note: apps.seen.<name> (v1.4) names the app by one lowercase label, the exe name without .exe.

transcripts/supervisor/outside-app-missi.note: An outside problem (app closed, busy port) is shown in the module's panels and retried; the module stays running and no crash is counted (v1.4).

facts/supervisor-facts.json.note: module.<id>.restart {delay_s, crash, of} or null, and module.<id>.recovery start-again | defaults | go-back (v1.4).
